title: Toyota - Wikipedia
content: # Toyota. While still a department of Toyota Industries, the company developed its first product, the Type A engine, in 1934 and its first passenger car in 1936, the Toyota AA. In the 1960s, Toyota took advantage of the rapidly growing Japanese economy to sell cars to a growing middle-class, leading to the development of the Toyota Corolla, which became the world's all-time best-selling automobile. The booming economy also funded an international expansion that allowed Toyota to grow into one of the largest automakers in the world, the largest company in Japan and the ninth-largest company in the world by revenue, as of December 2020. Toyota was the world's first automobile manufacturer to produce more than 10 million vehicles per year, a record set in 2012, when it also reported the production of its 200 millionth vehicle. Toyota was praised for being a leader in the development and sales of more fuel-efficient hybrid electric vehicles, starting with the introduction of the original Toyota Prius "Toyota Prius (XW10)") in 1997.

title: Toyota Motor Corp | Encyclopedia.com
content: In 1933 a Japanese man named Kiichiro Toyoda traveled to America where he visited a number of automobile production plants. Upon his return to Japan, the young man established an automobile division within his father’s loom manufactory and in May 1935 produced his first prototype vehicle. This was followed in 1940 by the establishment of the Toyoda Science Research Center (the nucleus of today’s Toyota Central Research and Development Laboratories, Inc.) and the Toyoda Works (presently Aichi Steel’ Works, Ltd.). title: Toyota Motor Corporation | Business and Management - EBSCO
content: Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi, Japan, is a leading global automobile manufacturer known for its diverse range of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and hybrids. It became the world's largest automaker in 2008 and remains a significant player in the automotive industry, employing over 370,000 individuals and producing more than 200 million vehicles since its inception. Toyota is recognized for pioneering the hybrid vehicle market with the introduction of the Prius in 1997, which was the first mass-produced hybrid automobile. Toyota's impact extends beyond manufacturing; it plays a significant role in the global economy and has strategic partnerships, such as its collaboration with Mazda. title: History of Toyota | Toyota Motor Corporation Official Global Website
content: # History of Toyota. Ever since its founding, Toyota has pursued business activities centered on the production and sale of automobiles, with the aim of contributing to a more prosperous society. Here, we introduce Toyota's history from its founding to the present day. ## The Beginnings. Taking on the Automotive Business -Setting Course to Enter Automotive Business-. From 1937 -Establishment of Toyota Motor Co., Ltd.-. 1940s -Automobile Prototypes, Research and Development of Basic Technology-. 1950s -Business Management Crisis (Labor dispute); Establishment of Toyota Motor Sales Co., Ltd.-. ## Inheritance and Evolution. 1960s -Mass Production Systems Established; Development of Mass-market Vehicle-. 1970s -Satisfying Public Needs (Emissions standards, Oil crisis)-. 1980s -Sales and Manufacturing Operations Merged to Form Toyota Motor Corporation; Full-scale Overseas Production Launched-. 1990s -Response to Environmental and Safety Issues-. 2000s -Rapid Expansion of Globalization-.
